title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 54-57 of the manuscript). Grothendieck is axiomatizing 'ateliers spatiaux'. An atelier is an abstract set A of 'figures' carrying two relations: an incidence/support relation |∘|_A and an order ⊴_A. The model is a 'spatios' (Σ, ≤, c), a set of 'points' with an order (or ≪) and a symmetric relation c. In the model, a figure is X = (Φ, ρ) with Φ ⊂ Σ (presumably finite) and ρ an order on Φ; Figspatial(Σ) is the set of such figures. On p.55 he sets out to prove axiom Atspat 3, a 'realizability' axiom. Step one: build from |∘|_A alone a space Σ_A, a quotient or set of supports. Step two: build from |∘|_A and ⊴_A a map Dév_A : A → Figspatial(Σ_A), the 'développement' of a figure. Step three: show that when A ⊂ Figspatial(Σ) satisfies Abspat 1-2, this construction gives back Σ and the tautological inclusion.

On p.55 he uses α: A → Σ, X ↦ X° (the extremal element of Φ for ρ), and β: Σ → P(A), S ↦ {X | X° ≤ S}. These induce mutually inverse bijections Σ_A ≅ Σ_Σ, and Σ_Σ ≅ Σ via supp°_Σ.

On this page (p.56) he factors Dév_A as A → P(Σ_A) → P(Σ), with X = (Φ, ρ) ↦ {supp°_A(X') | X' ∈ X̃ = Φ}. The arrow carries a '?' and the word 'fidèle?', so whether the map is faithful is left open. In the margin he notes that Dév_A X is moreover equipped with an order relation. Under Σ_A ≅ Σ_Σ, supp°_A(x') becomes supp°_Σ(x'). Under Σ_Σ ← Σ, this is just x'. So the image of X is Φ itself, and the transported order is ρ, via the identity X̃ → Φ. Hence Dév_A recovers the inclusion A ⊂ Figspatial(Σ) ('On gagne!').

The Scholie draws the conclusion. Giving a spatial atelier is equivalent to giving a spatios (Σ, ≤ or ≪, c) together with a subset A ⊂ Figspatial(Σ) satisfying the two conditions Abspat 1, 2 of p.54. This is a representation (reconstruction) theorem: the abstract incidence-and-order structure on figures determines the underlying point space, and the figures can be realized concretely as ordered subsets of points. The next page begins a category of sets with symmetric relations, whose morphisms are compatible correspondences E → P(E'), in order to make this functorial.
errors: Notational slippage: supp°_A is defined on elements of A (figures), but here it is applied to X' ∈ X̃ = Φ, which are points of Σ. Implicitly a point x' is identified with a degenerate figure (or with its class in Σ_A). This needs Abspat 1-2 to guarantee that points occur as figures in A, or are determined by them; this is not spelled out on this page.

The injectivity ('fidèle?') of A → P(Σ_A) is left with a question mark. What is actually proved is the identification with the given inclusion in the concrete case, not a general faithfulness statement.
Previous page: X° is described as the 'plus grand élément' of Φ for ρ, which presupposes that ρ has a greatest element (Φ nonempty, and either totally ordered or having a top). This is implicit.

ideas.what: Reconstruction of the point-space Σ from an abstract set of figures with support/incidence relation, via Σ_A ≅ Σ_Σ ≅ Σ
ideas.modern_name: representation/reconstruction theorem for incidence structures (cf. recovering points as atoms or supports; Stone-type duality)
ideas.usually_credited_to: general idea classical (Stone 1936; incidence-geometry foundations); this specific 'atelier/spatios' formalism appears unique to Grothendieck

ideas.what: Scholie: an atelier spatial is equivalent to a spatios (Σ, ≤/≪, c) plus a family A ⊂ Figspatial(Σ) satisfying Abspat 1, 2
ideas.modern_name: equivalence of an abstract axiomatic structure with a concrete 'space + admissible figures' structure (a structure/representation theorem)

ideas.what: Développement map Dév_A sending a figure to the ordered set of supports of its constituents
ideas.modern_name: realization/nerve-like functor from abstract figures to ordered subsets of points

missed.claim: A completed equivalence (scholie) between 'ateliers spatiaux' and spatios equipped with a family of spatial figures satisfying two axioms. It belongs to Grothendieck's 1986 program on the foundations of geometry (spatios, ateliers), which is essentially absent from the literature.
missed.quote: La donnée d'un atelier spatial revient à celle d'un spatios (Σ, ≤, c), muni de la structure supplémentaire définie par une A ⊂ Figspatial(Σ), satisfaisant les deux conditions Abspat 1, 2
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It documents an unpublished axiomatic approach to geometric figures, with points reconstructed from incidence data. It could interest work on synthetic/incidence geometry and the foundations of tame or discrete geometry. The individual proof on this page, however, is a routine verification.

missed.claim: Faithfulness of A → P(Σ_A) (whether a figure is determined by its developed ordered support set) is flagged with '?' and not settled on this page.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It would be needed for the abstract-to-concrete direction of the equivalence in full generality.

deep.surprise_reason: This is part of a little-known, unpublished Grothendieck formalism (ateliers/spatios), and it ends in a clean equivalence scholie. The mathematics on the page, however, is a routine reconstruction check of Stone/incidence type.
transcription_corrections: 'Abspat 1, 2' is probably the same axiom family as 'Atspat' on p.55 (or a variant 'Abspat' of p.54). The image reads roughly 'Abspat 1, 2 p. 54'.
Margin likely reads: 'les[?] pour l'instant — pourvu Dév_A X munis de relations d'ordre, soit Dév_A X'. Uncertain, but it signals that the developed figure carries an order.
Over the arrow: 'Dév!_A' and '+P(Σ_A)' as an insertion, replacing a crossed-out P(...).
